page.title: Testing your charts
page.description: Test a chart's retries and timeouts in milliseconds: your test answers each of its sends and moves a simulated clock.

hero.headline: Test an hour of timeouts in milliseconds
hero.lede: A payment that retries every 30 seconds runs all three attempts in a test that takes milliseconds. The test answers the chart's sends and moves its clock.

section.heading: Replace the chart's services and its clock
section.p: A chart reaches the world only through sends. The host passes each send to a handler you give it, an I/O processor.

item.term: The test's handlers stand in for the services.
item.text: They record what the chart sent and answer when the case needs it, with an error, or never.

item.term: A SimulatedClock moves only when the test moves it.
item.text: A timeout of an hour takes no time.

item.term: await host.idle() returns when the host has nothing left to do.
item.text: Assertions after it see everything the inputs before it did by the clock's time.

section.p: To check properties over generated runs instead of single cases, read .

section.heading: Check each step of a retrying payment
section.p: This chart charges a card, retries when no answer comes within 30 seconds, and gives up after the third attempt. Its test moves the clock 30 seconds at a time and checks each charge.

example.code: ok: retries, then gives up ok: an answer ends it

section.p: The second case answers with payment.send('charged'), as the handler's send.answer('charged') would, without the sendid. A handler may answer just as well.
Read the actor's state with actor.state() after an idle(): it reads the host as it is when called ().
Give the actor a name to see it end: a final state frees the name, so host.actor(name) throws StaleError.

section.heading: Step to each deadline to see every tick
section.p: clock.increment(ms) moves the clock once. What is due by then runs once, at the new time, and a delay it starts counts from there.
So a chart that ticks every second ticks once for an increment(3500), and its next tick is due a second later. Stepping by host.nextDeadline, the milliseconds to the next deadline, logs every tick:

example.code: tick 1 at 3500 tick 2 at 4500 tick 3 at 5500 tick 4 at 6500

section.heading: Await idle before you move the clock
section.p: actor.send returns before the actor handles the event, which it does later, at the clock's time then. Until then host.nextDeadline holds no deadline the event starts.
So an event sent just before an increment runs after the clock moved, and a delay it starts counts from there:

example.code: nextDeadline right after the input: undefined reserved at 59000 reserved at 59000 expired at 119000 expired at 119000

section.p: Both holds came due at 119000, though the first was sent at 0. Await idle() after each event whose effect the next step or assertion needs.

section.heading: On the real clock, await the actor's result
section.p: On the real clock, await host.idle() returns while a timeout is still pending. It waits only for work due now and for promises your handlers returned.
await actor.done waits instead for the actor's top-level final state, and settles with its <donedata>. await actor.ask(event, data) sends an event and settles with the chart's reply:

example.code: asked: progress 0 after idle(): still running done: all done

section.p: ask gives the event an origin the host answers itself. The chart replies with <send targetexpr="_event.origin">, as to another actor, and the promise settles with the reply's event name and data.
To give up on an ask, pass an AbortSignal as ask(event, data, { signal }). The ask rejects with the signal's reason, and a later reply is dropped.
A host closed while an ask waits leaves it pending for ever, as it leaves the promise of actor.state().

section.heading: Start each test from a snapshot
section.p: Set up a host once and take host.snapshot(). Each test then starts with Host.restore of it, the same actors in the same states ().

section.heading: Run the tests in QuickJS too
section.p: When production runs your charts in QuickJS, run each test a second time with datamodel: 'quickjs' on the host ().

section.heading: Fail the test on a handler's error
section.p: A handler that throws makes the next await host.idle() reject, which fails the test (Errors).
A host given onHandlerError reports the error there instead. Collect what it receives and assert the list is empty.

section.heading: Close every host in teardown
section.p: Call host.close() in a finally or the test framework's teardown. A forgotten host on a SimulatedClock lets the process exit, but holds its memory until collected.
